newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to give miners 650 bln rbls to stop strike.
newsitem.headline: Russia to give miners 650 bln rbls to stop strike.

text.p: The Russian government will make available a further 650 billion roubles for coal miners this month to put an end to the strike launched by almost 400,000 workers across Russia, a top cabinet minister said on Thursday.
The government has already transferred 300 billion roubles of this sum and the rest will be paid by December 27, First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin told a news conference.

If the government manages to get a $250 million credit from the World Bank, which is currently under negotiation, the coal sector would receive almost all the 10.4 trillion roubles budgeted for the industry for 1996, he said.
Yuri Malyshev, president of OAO Rossiiskaya Ugolnaya Kompaniya (Rossugol), which unites most of Russia's coal mines, said he was satisfied by the decision.
"Such a decision makes the issue less contentious and we can conduct talks with the trade unions about stopping the strike," he said. "We think the problem will soon be resolved."
He added he expected the credit agreement with the World Bank to be signed on December 10.
Malyshev said the coal industry had so far received only 5.29 trillion roubles of the 10.4 trillion in subsidies provided for in the 1996 budget.
He said the government would forgive mines 400 billion roubles in taxes.
Consumers owed the industry 7.5 trillion roubles, he added.
Wage arrears in the industry amounted to 2.47 trillion roubles on October 20, the government said in a statement, and the industry's other debts exceed 20.4 trillion roubles.
Since the start of reconstruction in the coal sector in 1993, the government has closed 50 unprofitable mines and plans to close over 60 more soon, Potanin said.
Government subsidies to the coal industry have fallen to 15 percent from 80 percent before 1993, he said.
